title: Ceuta Braces for Morocco's Election-Day Crossing Call as ~9,000 Migrants Remain, Including Up to 700 Minors on Streets
detail: More than seven weeks after the July 30-31 mass crossing, roughly 9,000 migrants remained in Ceuta as of Sep 22 — about 6,000 housed in government-run facilities and up to 3,000 still on the streets or beaches, including 500-700 unaccompanied minors mixed among roughly 2,000 minors now in shelter services. Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares said social media calls circulating for a fresh mass crossing on Sep 23, timed to Morocco's legislative elections, did not 'seem to be gaining significant traction,' while Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska announced reinforced Civil Guard deployments in Ceuta as a precaution. Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres reiterated that minors 'cannot be returned overnight' to Morocco, as roughly 600 family-reunification cases remained stalled awaiting a Moroccan response and opposition-run autonomous communities continued resisting mainland transfers of unaccompanied minors.

media.caption: Security forces on alert near the Ceuta border ahead of Morocco's Sep 23 legislative elections

title: Torres Blames PP for Stranded Ceuta Minors, Announces New 700-Place Camp, Reports 2,321 Registered
detail: Speaking after the Sep 22 Council of Ministers, Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres escalated the government's dispute with Ceuta president Juan Jesús Vivas over unaccompanied minors, saying 'if today a thousand minors remain on Ceuta's streets, it is because the PP wants it that way' and accusing the PP and Vox of blocking mainland transfers for political leverage ahead of a Sep 26 PP/Vox-backed demonstration demanding early elections. Torres put the total unaccompanied-minor count at 2,321 registered (filiados) — up from roughly 1,478 registered as of Sep 1 — with about 6,000 adults and 2,000 minors already in government facilities and estimates ranging 500-1,000 minors still unaccounted for on the streets. He also reported 6,791 migrants had voluntarily returned to Morocco and 318 had been expelled since the Aug 10 return program began, up from 5,482 returns as of Sep 15, and announced a new 500-700 place reception facility at the Cuesta Caballería site, expected to open within days. Vox's Ceuta spokesperson accused Torres of hypocrisy for not housing minors in his own home, while Ceuta's government continued withholding authorisation for mainland minor transfers.

media.caption: Minister Ángel Víctor Torres announces a new reception camp for minors amid the dispute with Ceuta's government
